messages.content:
You write the two short notices Ryde sends after a dispute ruling: one to the rider, one to the driver.
Each ≤ 120 words, plain English, second person, no legalese: state the outcome, the one or two facts that decided it,
the amount and how it is paid (Ryde voucher), and what it means for the recipient (e.g. account review). Do not cite
ids like F3 or RD-2. If the case was escalated to a human reviewer, say only that and what the reviewer will look at —
do not state a conclusion and do not promise a timeframe (the routing notice carries the service level). Return JSON: {"rider": "...", "driver": "..."}

Case B-0001. Final outcome: refund_partial, amount $4.33 as a Ryde voucher. Account flag: no. Recommended action: Refund $4.33 (voucher) for the 3.07 km unexcused detour on segment F3; no account flag..
Reasoning:
RydeTAXI is metered, so extra distance directly enters the fare [F6]; the trip's own rate is distance fare ÷ distance km [RD-2]. One off-route segment is on record: 09:24–09:30, 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, adding 3.07 km [F3][RD-1].

Checking exemptions: no traffic incident supports the detour — the trace shows the RD-4(a) screen fails, the only traffic facts are speed band 5 (40–49 km/h, i.e. free-flowing) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard and no incidents near the route [F11][F12][F13][RD-4]; a band record cannot exempt on its own, and fair weather removes any other "reasonable cause" [F14][RD-4(c)]. No rider-requested stop is measured in the segment [F3][RD-3].

RD-5 consent: the chat is complete and fully timestamped, 2 messages — the rider's pickup message at 09:04 and the driver's arrival message at 09:05 — neither of which touches the route [F7][F8][F9]. The only route account is the driver's post-trip statement that "the GPS rerouted", which is not a rider message sent before 09:24:50 and is a claim, not consent [F10][RD-5][G11]. So no agreement covers this segment; the segment counts [RD-5].

Amount: rate = $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.4101/km; 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.3290, rounded to $4.33 [F4][F6][F3][RD-2]. This is the refundable distance only; the rider's broader "$3.2 km extra" figure of $4.51 exceeds the measured detour and is not the policy amount [F4][RD-2]. RD-6 flag is not triggered: the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but it is not a route dispute (route: 0), so there is no prior upheld route breach [F16][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint in full — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears; this is a fare/route dispute [F7][F8][F10][F13][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the segment is measured, the chat record is complete and timestamped, and the fare record carries both distance and distance fare, settling every element the ruling needs [F3][F6][F9][RD-2][RD-5].

function.name: final_result
function.description: The final response which ends this conversation

function.name: final_result
function.arguments: {"rider": "We reviewed your dispute and you're getting a partial refund. We measured a 3.07 km detour on your trip where the driver went 3.78 km instead of the 0.71 km direct route. We have no record of your agreeing to a different route, and no traffic problem or stop of yours explains it, so that extra distance counts. You'll receive $4.33 as a Ryde voucher. Your account is not affected. Thanks for flagging it.", "driver": "We reviewed a route dispute on one of your trips. We measured a 3.07 km detour: 3.78 km driven versus 0.71 km on the direct route. We found nothing on record showing the rider agreed to a different route beforehand, and no traffic incident or rider-requested stop explains it, so the segment was not exempt. The rider is receiving $4.33 back as a Ryde voucher. No flag is being added to your account; this is a fare-only correction. No further action is needed from you."}
